headline: A Living Index of Hacker News Books
lede: HackerBooks turns years of scattered comment references into a browsable reading index. Its 15,766 entries link back to the conversations that surfaced them, with randomized discovery and downloadable data for further tinkering.

headline: Postgres Slows Down to Find More Bugs
lede: AI-assisted testing is uncovering defects faster than PostgreSQL’s maintainers can safely absorb them. The delayed 19 release makes a sober case for treating discovery, review, and compatibility as the work—not merely obstacles to shipping.
pullquote: A slower release is the price of seeing what mature software has been hiding.

headline: Wikipedia, Reassembled from HN Links
lede: Wikihack turns the encyclopedia’s appearances on Hacker News into a wandering discovery feed. Browse the most-linked, randomly surfaced, or newly rising topics, then follow each thread back to its original discussion.

headline: A Quieter Way to Browse Video
lede: HackerTube gathers 6,454 videos from recommendations made in nearly 40,000 Hacker News comments. The result is less a new platform than a reflection on how carefully chosen context can make online discovery feel human again.

headline: Syscall.sh Maps Linux Across Architectures
lede: A refreshed syscall.sh exposes Linux system calls by architecture and kernel version. Search the tables, inspect calling conventions and history, or pull the underlying JSON when the ABI needs to meet a toolchain.

headline: How Berkeley Began Building BSD
lede: In 1977, Berkeley’s first BSD release bundled Pascal and ex atop an AT&T Unix license. The illustrated history follows the small tools, patient ports, and practical distribution work that carried Berkeley Unix toward 3BSD and DARPA’s attention.

headline: Bones Signal the Body to Age Slowly
lede: In mice, mechanically stressed bone cells release factors including PEDF that improve organ health and extend late-life survival. The result offers a plausible biological account of exercise’s benefits, while leaving human efficacy and safety firmly unresolved.

headline: The Smart TV That Never Calls Home
lede: A large screen need not become another networked sensor. The practical design is quiet: leave the television offline, route streaming through HDMI, and treat microphones, telemetry, and advertising layers as optional machinery—not inevitable features.

headline: The Grid’s One-Minute Mystery
lede: Battery systems were quietly checking their state of charge at the start of every minute—and doing it together. Across 80 devices, that synchronized demand produced measurable grid-frequency dips that randomized timing could largely smooth away.

headline: HackerHack Opens Another Door to HN
lede: HackerHack reorganizes Hacker News posts into a separate browsing layer, without AI and without abandoning the site’s familiar shape. It is a small information-retrieval experiment in making old discussions easier to find without pretending the archive is new.
